title: Bounded coherent complexes on Noetherian schemes are pseudo-coherent
statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Every object of D(\mathcal O_S) [def-pc-derived-category] with bounded coherent cohomology is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.10.3 (Tag 08E8; label lemma-identify-pseudo-coherent-noetherian)

proof.text: Choose integers $a\le b$ such that $H^i(E)=0$ for $i<a$ and for $i>b$; this is exactly the boundedness hypothesis on the coherent cohomology of $E$.

For every $i\in[a,b]$, $H^i(E)$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module and $S$ is Noetherian, so the existing coherent-sheaf lemma [lem-sc-coherent-pseudo-coherent] makes $H^i(E)$, and hence $H^i(E)[-i]$, pseudo-coherent: shifts preserve the local bounded-above finite-free condition in [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Tag 08E8, lemma-identify-pseudo-coherent-noetherian, proof via coherent cohomology sheaves

proof.text: For $m=b,b-1,\dots,a$, apply the truncation node [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle] with $n=-m$: it gives a distinguished triangle $H^m(E)[-m]\to\tau_{\ge m}E\to\tau_{\ge m+1}E\to H^m(E)[-m+1]$. Since $H^i(E)=0$ for $i>b$, the standard t-structure description [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] identifies $\tau_{\ge b+1}E$ with the zero object. Descending induction on $m$ now proves $\tau_{\ge m}E$ pseudo-coherent: the right term $\tau_{\ge m+1}E$ is pseudo-coherent by the previous induction step (or zero at $m=b$), the left term $H^m(E)[-m]$ is pseudo-coherent by Step 2, and [lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-distinguished-triangle] gives the middle term. At $m=a$, the vanishing $H^i(E)=0$ for $i<a$ and the same standard truncation characterization identify $\tau_{\ge a}E$ with $E$, so $E$ is pseudo-coherent.
